content:
Channing Tatum wants to clarify that he is not the mastermind behind an Instagram account dedicated to mocking his former fiancée Zoë Kravitz.

On Monday, the actor, who appeared in "Avengers: Doomsday," denied the rumours, saying he does not use the "finsta" account @bidness_nonya to take digs at Kravitz and her new fiancé Harry Styles. Fans had started to suspect over the weekend that he was the person behind the account.

The rumour gained traction after internet users noticed that Tatum appeared to be the account's only follower, and the account has now been deactivated or deleted.

The account had a history of leaving snarky comments on Kravitz's and Styles's posts, including once commenting under a related post, "Just here for the hate."

"Yo, I truly can't believe people think I have nothing better to do than be on this app pouring honey on myself y'all. This is so funny," Tatum wrote in a response on his Instagram Story. "Also if I did wanna have a finsta, I mean come on get out of here, would I follow myself? You think I'm that stupid?"

The actor added, "Guys come on now. But if you do truly need me to say it, I only have one IG account and it's @channingtatum."

Cosmopolitan reported that the true holder of the mysterious account actually once told a follower online directly, "I'm not (Tatum)."

HuffPost has reached out to Tatum, Kravitz and Styles for comment.

Tatum and Kravitz were first romantically linked in August 2021, when they worked together on Kravitz's directorial debut, "Blink Twice." They got engaged in 2023 but called off their wedding plans in October 2024.

People magazine confirmed Styles and Kravitz are engaged after eight months of dating, with the news coming in April. Kravitz was previously photographed kissing her boyfriend in London while wearing a large diamond ring on her left ring finger. A source told the magazine that the couple only shared the news with a small circle of close friends and family.

Tatum is reportedly now dating Australian model Inka Williams.
